Here $d$ is the number of transform axes

gaps.note: The table gives the normalized cost dK for prefix moves, but the page never says what a prefix move is or why it costs dK per bit. The paper (around line 4930) derives it from O(dK) linear scans in the synthetic-transform cost lemma; the page only derives the chunk-exchange and simultaneous-round rows.

The row d^2(1+l^tau) is stated without derivation. It comes from O(d^2) adjacent axis moves each costing O(V(1+l^tau)) (peeling one excess bit, exchanging equal-width parts), which the page does not mention.

The row dp^delta is given with no account of how chirps are computed or why they cost d p^delta per coefficient. The paper derives it from products on O(p)-bit numerators with the O(N log N) multiplier, costing O(d p^{1+delta}) per entry.

The page gives no reason that p^{A+C} visits-times-setup is o(V). The paper needs that r exceeds every fixed power of p, so that setup per record or per line is o(Tp). The page does not say what is cited or why it applies.

gaps.quote: Repairing the fraction $O(d2^{-K})$ of exceptional addresses costs $o(V)$
gaps.note: The page never says what the exceptional addresses are, where they arise, or how they are repaired. It also does not say why the fraction O(d 2^{-K}) gives o(V): the paper sorts the exceptional stream with O(p) scans over up to p^A visits, giving O(V p^{A'} 2^{-K}), which is o(V) because 2^{-K} beats any power of p when K = Theta(p^{epsilon c}).
